messages:
Maya (CS): Heads-up — VoltWave onboarding: p95 spikes and token cost drift on their chat endpoint. Renewal flagged if we don't show a clear plan by Friday. Looking for quick, low-risk perf levers (quant + routing) we can push as a proactive ops recommendation.
Priya (Solutions): Can we do a targeted quant canary + routing tweak to a lower-latency pool? small cohort first (1% traffic) so we can measure quality and cost delta.
Diego (ML Eng): I can run an int8 and q4_0 profile locally against their eval set. Risk: hallucination/safety changes possible with aggressive quant. Suggest compare EXACT nll/bertscore on 1k prompts.
Liam (SRE): Routing note — their traffic comes from eu-west primarily. We have a spare regional replica in eu-west-1 that has lower tail latency. We can route a canary to that replica with a fallback to us-east if p99 > 1.0s. Need a rollout policy and feature flag.
Maya (CS): Ideal outcome: 20-30% token cost reduction or 10-20% p95 improvement with no >1% quality regression. If we can commit a short-term dedicated burst for the canary, that helps.
Priya (Solutions): Quick config I recommend for canary (1% traffic):
```json
{
  "route": "eu-west-1-canary",
  "model": "redwood-open-7b-q4_0",
  "quant_profile": "q4_0",
  "prefix_cache": false,
  "traffic_pct": 1
}
```
Diego (ML Eng): For quality checks, use this eval slice: 500 high-context convo prompts + 200 safety-sensitive cases. I'll automate the diff metrics and post before/after. If we see >1% drop on exact-match or major safety regressions, we rollback immediately.
Liam (SRE): I'll create a rollout policy with these circuit-breakers: p99 > 1.0s OR error rate > 0.5% triggers auto-fallback to primary model/region. Also adding an alert to #eng-oncall.
ops-bot: [alert] VoltWave chat endpoint p95 spike detected — auto-ticket created (#CS-4891).
Maya (CS): Thanks. Diego — can you estimate how long to get the q4_0 run and evaluation? Priya — can you coordinate with VoltWave for a short enablement session and ask them to freeze prompt set during canary?
Priya (Solutions): I can do a 30-min enablement tomorrow 10am PT. I'll ask them to stop config changes and share a canned 1k prompt set.
Diego (ML Eng): I can have baseline vs q4_0 diffs in ~6 hours once I get the prompt pack. Will post the metrics and a short summary of any tokenization differences.
Liam (SRE): Allocated eu-west-1-canary pool temporarily. Adding fallback route + SLO guardrails. Will annotate runbook.
Maya (CS): If canary looks good we propose a 2-week pilot with measured billing impact and a renewal-friendly summary: expected savings, measured latency improvements, and QA matrix. That should defuse renewal risk.
Priya (Solutions): I'll capture feedback and prepare a one-pager for the customer: what changed, why, rollback criteria, and next steps.
Diego (ML Eng): One heads-up: if we need more aggressive savings later we can try a mixed-precision hop (int8 for decoding, q3 for attention) but only after we validate.
Maya (CS): Great. Action items: Diego — run eval + post metrics (due in 6h). Liam — set rollout policy & alerts (done). Priya — enablement call + prompt pack (tomorrow 10am PT). I'll update CS renewal thread with this plan.
Liam (SRE): tagging @eng-oncall so they're aware during canary window.
ops-bot: [ticket update] CS-4891 assigned to Maya.
Maya (CS): Appreciated everyone. If all goes well, we'll propose a 90-day pilot tied to a renewal concession (discounted reserved capacity) — will discuss with RevOps after metrics are in.
Priya (Solutions): I'll note the concession request and prep pricing scenarios.
Diego (ML Eng): Posting first diff now: q4_0 cost -22%, p95 -12%, quality delta: exact-match drop 0.7% (within threshold). Uploading graphs to the thread.
Maya (CS): That's promising. Please include a short blurb on which prompts regressed. We need transparency for the customer.
Priya (Solutions): I'll draft the customer-facing summary and circulate.
Liam (SRE): Will keep the fallback ready for immediate rollback.
Maya (CS): Closing loop later today after the enablement. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
